market.question: Will Trump officially rename AI before Oct 1, 2026? (Before Oct 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If Donald Trump formally adopts or directs adoption of a replacement name for Artificial Intelligence or AI for United States official use through a personally signed presidential action after Issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The qualifying action must be of the specific type designated (executive order, presidential memorandum, proclamation, directive, determination, or finding), be signed by the President personally during the specified time period, and explicitly address the topic in the document's operative provisions, title, or official White House summary. Actions must have legal or policy effect - ceremonial proclamations without policy impact do not qualify unless specifically included. Actions that only incidentally mention the topic, statements without formal action, actions by cabinet members, legislative proposals without executive action, and signing statements do not qualify. The action must be publicly announced or documented by a Source Agency before expiration.

The topic is the preexisting official designation Artificial Intelligence or AI for United States official use. Any replacement name qualifies. The action must adopt or direct adoption of the replacement for United States official use; an informal, honorary, or agency-only label does not qualify.

recent_facts.fact: On Tuesday, Sept 29, 2026, Trump said he would sign a 'very powerful' executive order at 5 p.m. that day renaming artificial intelligence 'superintelligence.' He said, 'I spoke to President Xi; he loves it.' The article does not confirm that the order was signed.

After a White House luncheon with tech executives, Trump said: 'We're going to be signing a document today at about 5 o'clock, renaming artificial intelligence because it's not artificial... officially renaming it superintelligence.'
Reports from Sept 29 say the executive order had not yet been signed. Trump said it would make 'SI' the official term across federal documents.

The announcement came alongside the launch of a new America.gov website that uses AI to simplify access to federal services. Trump called it 'a preview of what is possible with superintelligence or SI, and that's the official name in the United States.'

At the UN General Assembly on Sept 22, 2026, Trump said: 'From this point forward, all of United States documents... will be changed to use the much more accurate term super, as opposed to artificial.' This was a spoken announcement, not a signed order. The article said the White House had not yet announced how it would be implemented.

On Sept 22, several outlets reported Trump saying AI would be renamed 'super intelligence' in all US documents. Trump had floated several other names in earlier weeks before choosing superintelligence.
The signing was scheduled for 5 p.m. on Sept 29, 2026. The question closes at 2026-10-01T03:59Z (11:59 p.m. ET on Sept 30), leaving about 1.5 days for signing and publication by a Source Agency.

To count, the action must be a presidential action personally signed by Trump that adopts or directs a replacement name for AI for US official use, and it must be publicly documented before the close. The Sept 22 UN speech alone is a statement without formal action and does not qualify.

Precedent: In 2025, Trump followed through on announced renamings with signed actions. Examples are the executive order restoring the 'Department of War' as a secondary name (Sept 5, 2025) and the 'Gulf of America' order (Jan 20, 2025), each signed within days to weeks of public talk about it.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of September 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. On September 24 Trump barred CNN from Air Force One.

A Daily Kos community post titled "Little Sensitive Piggy" was published on September 21, 2026. The article text could not be retrieved, and nothing available shows that Trump himself said "piggy" at the time.
The White House defended Trump calling Bloomberg reporter Catherine Lucey "piggy" on Air Force One in November 2025. That remark is his main widely reported use of the word as an insult.
In the days after the "piggy" remark, Trump insulted other female reporters with words like "ugly," "stupid" and "terrible person." These reports do not show him repeating "piggy."

Trump has long called the US a "piggy bank" on trade. At a May 2019 rally in Panama City Beach he called America "the piggy bank that everybody wants to rob." Saying "piggy bank" would include the word "piggy."

At the June 2018 G7 summit, Trump said the US is "the piggy bank that everybody's robbing." He has used the "piggy bank" phrase repeatedly when talking about trade and tariffs, including a later post about foreign digital taxes making Silicon Valley the world's "piggy bank" (Gizmodo).

About two days are left before the deadline of October 1, 2026 at 12:00am ET. Any public remark, published direct quote or Truth Social or X post by Trump counts, and so do plural or possessive forms.

market.question: Will the U.S. and China agree to establish an AI hotline before Oct 1, 2026? (Before Oct 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If the governments of the United States and China have formally announced an agreement to establish, or have implemented, a bilateral notification mechanism for AI incidents that could affect national security after Issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify, unless the new article itself explicitly reaffirms the truth of the topic as of the publication date. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

A qualifying mechanism must be a government-to-government arrangement for notifying the other government about relevant AI incidents; general AI dialogue, shared principles, safety cooperation, or a general hotline without the incident-notification function does not satisfy this topic.

The mechanism must be expressly described in an official government announcement, agreement text, or qualifying Source Agency report as covering AI incidents with national-security implications. A general AI-incident channel does not qualify based solely on an inference that the incidents it covers could affect national security.

A formal announcement must appear in an official agreement text, communiqué, readout, press release, other written government statement, or a formal government press conference, briefing, leaders' summit, signing ceremony, or formal address. One government's official statement is sufficient only when it expressly states that both governments agreed. Informal remarks, press gaggles, a report of a proposal, an agreement to meet, or a transcript of those remarks alone does not qualify.

Implementation requires evidence that both governments have operationalized, activated, or used the bilateral notification mechanism. A unilateral proposal, ongoing negotiation, planned dialogue, generic AI-safety principles, company standards, private or unofficial arrangement, domestic-only system, or a mechanism unrelated to AI incidents affecting national security does not qualify. A broader AI-safety agreement qualifies only when it expressly adopts or implements this incident-notification component.

recent_facts.fact: Jackson Koivun is in the field for the 2026 Bank of Utah Championship at Black Desert Resort in Ivins, Utah, which runs October 1-4. He is ranked No. 57 in the world, the 5th-highest-ranked player in the field. The players ranked above him are Michael Brennan (32), Maverick McNealy (48), Marco Penge (53) and Matt Wallace (54).
The field has about 120 players, and 24 of them are in the world top 100. The purse is $6 million. The course is a 7,421-yard par 71.

Koivun went 2-0-1 in his Presidents Cup debut at Medinah, which ended September 27. He beat Si Woo Kim 2 and 1 in Sunday singles and was the only American who did not lose a match. The U.S. won the Cup.
In his last start before the Presidents Cup, Koivun tied for 5th at the Biltmore Championship Asheville at 21 under. Jacob Bridgeman won that event at 26 under (258).
Koivun won the 3M Open in his third professional start. He finished at 25 under (259) and beat world No. 1 Scottie Scheffler by three strokes.

Koivun turned pro in summer 2026 through PGA Tour University's accelerated program. His 2026 results include a missed cut at the John Deere Classic (his pro debut), the 3M Open win, T23 at the U.S. Open (as an amateur), T10 at the ISCO Championship and T5 at the Biltmore. He won 11 individual college events at Auburn.
Koivun, 21, was the final captain's pick for the U.S. Presidents Cup team, chosen by captain Brandt Snedeker.

The event has been played twice before (2024 and 2025). Both winners were first-time PGA Tour winners who were not among the top-ranked players in the field: Matt McCarty in 2024, and Michael Brennan in 2025, a sponsor invite who won by four shots at 22 under (262) in his first PGA Tour start as a pro.
At the Biltmore Championship two weeks earlier, a comparable FedExCup Fall event, Koivun finished T5 and the winner was Jacob Bridgeman, who was earning his second win of the year.

The Bank of Utah Championship is a 72-hole FedExCup Fall event. The first round is October 1 and the final round is October 4, before the question closes on October 18. The tournament begins four days after the Presidents Cup ended.
If Koivun withdraws or does not tee off, the tournament-winner question resolves No. It resolves Yes only if he wins the event.

market.question: Will Spain win on 2026-10-03?
market.rules:
In the upcoming game, scheduled for October 3, 2026
If Spain wins, this market will resolve to "Yes".
Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".
If the game is postponed, this market will remain open until the game has been completed.
If the game is canceled entirely, with no make-up game, this market will resolve "No".
This market refers only to the outcome within the first 90 minutes of regular play plus stoppage time.

The primary resolution source for this market is the official statistics of the event as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. However, if the governing body or event organizers have not published final match statistics within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, data from Flashscore may be used; if Flashscore data is unavailable, data from Sofascore may be used; if neither is available, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead. All markets will settle based on the official final result as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

market.question: Will Russia enter Mykolaivka by September 30, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Mykolaivka, Donetsk Oblast, (48.854785° N, 37.770676° E) between market creation and the specified date (ET).

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

market.question: 0 ships transit Hormuz on any date by September 30?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a daily number of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to 0 for any date between market creation and the specified date, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No."

Transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF PortWatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a daily number of transit calls equal to 0, or once complete data has been published for the specified period without such a publication. If complete data for the specified period has not been published within 28 calendar days of the end of the specified period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data, and do not include cases where IMF PortWatch differs from alternative sources. Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying except in the case of data integrity issues. 

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

recent_facts.fact: The latest IMF PortWatch data point is for 2026-09-27, when 1 vessel transited the Strait of Hormuz. The pre-crisis baseline is about 85 per day. The brief does not report any zero-transit day in the recent data.
IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit through Hormuz on 2026-09-20. This was described as the lowest single-day count since the conflict began, apart from the zero days in March.
PortWatch has recorded 3 zero-transit days for Hormuz since 2026-03-01, all in March 2026 right after the strait was closed. The seven years of the series before that contain none.
IMF PortWatch recorded 8 transits on 2026-09-13 and 6 transits on 2026-09-06, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

IMF PortWatch publishes weekly, on Tuesdays, with about a two-day lag, so the newest Hormuz data is usually 2 to 9 days old. Data for 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-30 would be expected in the Tuesday 2026-10-06 update, which falls inside the market's 28-day window for complete data.

A non-PortWatch tracker counted 17 vessels transiting Hormuz on 2026-09-28 (11 inbound, 6 outbound), down from 24 the day before. It also noted that many tankers cross with their AIS transponders switched off.
A commodity-vessel tracker counted 10 crossings on 2026-09-23, up from 7 on 2026-09-22, against a 10-day average of about 17. Other trackers count differently from PortWatch.

An unidentified tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on 2026-09-28. Mediators were still pursuing a US-Iran deal, but Iran's UN delegation said it had no plans for more meetings, and US Ambassador Mike Waltz dismissed Iran's proposal.
A Kuwaiti KOTC tanker was reported struck in the Strait of Hormuz. US-Iran talks remain stalled after the US rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the strait.
In early September the US struck Iranian oil tankers for the first time, in retaliation for Iranian attacks, and the exchanges of fire in the strait continued through the month.

Late September was described as day 212-213 of the strait's closure. About 233 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, and war-risk premiums were about 40 times normal.
Between 2026-03-01 and 2026-07-19, IMF PortWatch recorded 1,400 Hormuz transits, a daily average of 9.9 compared with 103.2 in the same window of 2025.
PortWatch data for 2026-09-28, 09-29 and 09-30 is still unpublished. These are the last dates that count toward the question.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

market.question: Will the unemployment rate (U-3) be above 3.9% in September? (Above 3.9%)
market.rules: If the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (U-3) reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics in the Employment Situation Report is above 3.9% in September 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.

recent_facts.fact: The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for August 2026 was 4.1%, the same as July. The number of unemployed people changed little at 7.0 million.
The labor force participation rate was 61.6% in August 2026, down 0.5 percentage points since January.

The 2026 path of the unemployment rate was reported as: April 4.3%, May 4.3%, June 4.2%, July 4.1%, August 4.1%. That is a slow decline of about 0.1 point or less per month. Figures reported for January and February (4.7%) and March (4.3%) were not seasonally adjusted.
BLS reported that the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.3% in May 2026.
A year earlier, in September 2025, the unemployment rate was 4.4%.

Initial jobless claims were 197,000 for the week ending September 19, 2026, down 1,000. The 4-week average fell to 202,250. Prior weeks: 206,000 (Sept 5) and 196,000 (Sept 12), which is the survey reference week for the September household survey.
The September 2026 Employment Situation report is scheduled for Friday, October 2, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET (12:30 UTC). The question closes at 12:29 UTC that day.
Congress passed a continuing resolution extending federal funding past the September 30 deadline to December 11. The House vote was 370-48, so no shutdown should disrupt the October 2 BLS release.
Precedent: in the 2025 shutdown, the September 2025 report was delayed more than 6 weeks. The October 2025 household survey was never conducted, so no unemployment rate was published for that month.

BLS publishes the seasonally adjusted U-3 rate rounded to one decimal place. The threshold 'above 3.9%' means 4.0% or higher. From August's 4.1%, the rate would have to fall 0.2 points or more to resolve No.

The following rules govern the merging, joint contention, and splitting of listed parties:

- If Likud or Together (or any successor party created through a merger) merge with or contest the election jointly with any other party, the option corresponding to Likud or Together will represent the resultant candidate list or merged party. 

Otherwise:

- If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more unlisted parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list. If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more other listed parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the party which held the most seats in the prior Knesset will represent all seats won by the merged party/joint candidate list. If these rules do not adequately determine which option represents a merged party or joint candidate list, the listed party whose name, as listed in this market, comes first in alphabetical order, will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list.

- If a listed party splits into multiple parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent the resulting party that holds the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of the split. If these rules do not adequately determine which party represents a listed option after a split, the listed option will represent all seats won by the party resulting from the split whose primary English name comes first in alphabetical order.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The boundaries of the municipality are those shown under the “Ukrainian Settlements” layer on the ISW map.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded under a qualifying layer on the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

recent_facts.fact: India won the 1st ODI in Thiruvananthapuram by 8 wickets. West Indies made 295/7, including Justin Greaves' maiden ODI century, and Virat Kohli's 139* took India to the target in 41.4 overs. India lead the three-match series 1-0.

The 2nd ODI is a day-night match at Barsapara Cricket Stadium, Guwahati, on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, starting at 14:00 local time. It had not started as of today. India can wrap up the series with a win.

West Indies allrounder Justin Greaves, who scored 101 off 108 balls in the 1st ODI, has been ruled out of the Guwahati ODI with a calf injury he picked up in that match. Jewel Andrew could move up the order.
Sherfane Rutherford missed the 1st ODI for personal reasons and is set to rejoin the West Indies squad for the 2nd ODI.

India are without Jasprit Bumrah, who is away on Asian Games duty, and Hardik Pandya, who has not been cleared fit. They used three allrounders and only three specialist bowlers in the 1st ODI. Nitish Kumar Reddy, back from a left quadriceps injury, opened the bowling and struggled for rhythm.
Across 142 ODIs between the sides, India have won 72 and West Indies 64, with 2 ties and 4 no results. This appears to be the record before the 1st ODI of this series.

In ODIs played in India, India lead West Indies 32 wins to 28 across 61 matches, with 1 tie. Four of the five lowest team totals in this fixture belong to West Indies, including 104 all out at Thiruvananthapuram in 2018.

West Indies' last ODI win in India was by 8 wickets in Chennai on December 15, 2019. India have won every home ODI against West Indies since then, including the 2022 series and the 1st ODI on September 27, 2026.

recent_facts.fact: In West Indies' previous ODI series, at home against Sri Lanka in June–July 2026, Sri Lanka won 1-0. Sri Lanka won the 1st ODI by 41 runs, and the 2nd and 3rd ODIs were abandoned without a ball bowled.

market.question: Will Yashar win the most seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are expected to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party or coalition that wins the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of this election.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties or coalitions for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose candidate list received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed name appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Israeli Knesset.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Israel’s Central Election Committee (Va'adet HaBehirot HaMerkazit) (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/central-elections-committee/govil-landing-page).

The following rules govern the merging, joint contention, and splitting of listed parties:

- If Likud or Together (or any successor party created through a merger) merge with or contest the election jointly with any other party, the option corresponding to Likud or Together will represent the resultant candidate list or merged party. 

Otherwise:

- If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more unlisted parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list. If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more other listed parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the party which held the most seats in the prior Knesset will represent all seats won by the merged party/joint candidate list. If these rules do not adequately determine which option represents a merged party or joint candidate list, the listed party whose name, as listed in this market, comes first in alphabetical order, will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list.

- If a listed party splits into multiple parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent the resulting party that holds the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of the split. If these rules do not adequately determine which party represents a listed option after a split, the listed option will represent all seats won by the party resulting from the split whose primary English name comes first in alphabetical order.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $85 in September?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of September 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered. The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours.

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract's last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month).

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract's last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" and "Low" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.source: Investing.com (Crude Oil WTI Futures historical data)
recent_facts.fact: Investing.com's daily WTI futures data puts the lowest September 2026 low at $86.13, on September 1. Every other September session's low was $88.58 or higher. None of the daily lows for September 1–30 reached $85. This is continuous front-month data, not Pyth 1-minute candles.
Early on September 30, WTI futures were at $89.06, with a session range so far of $89.00–$89.06. That is about $4 (roughly 4.5%) above $85.
On September 29, WTI opened at $93.53 and traded between $94.72 and $88.58 before closing at $89.05. That $88.58 low was the lowest level since the September 1 session.

The August 31 session had a low of $84.11 and closed at $85.76. The September 1 session, which starts at 6 PM ET on August 31, opened at $86.31 and bottomed at $86.13. So the sub-$85 trade happened in an August session, before September's trading began.

On September 30, oil steadied after its biggest drop in more than a week. WTI was slipping toward $89 and Brent was near $103. Middle East crude exports had rebounded to 17.5 million barrels a day, 98% of pre-war levels.

On September 29, WTI fell about 3.5% to around $89.38 and Brent fell 2.6% to $102.59. The drop came as Saudi crude exports from its Red Sea ports recovered after an attack on a key pipeline earlier in the month.
On September 28, WTI settled at $92.60 after reaching $96.54 intraday. Prices came off their highs on reports that Saudi Arabia was ramping its East-West pipeline back up after repairs.

WTI's September peak was a high of $105.63 on September 16. The price then fell to around $89–92 in the last two weeks of the month, as U.S.-Iran truce hopes and a recovery in Saudi supply weighed on it.

Only one session is left: September 30, which ends at 5:00 PM ET. The market closes at 03:59:59 UTC on October 1, which is 11:59 PM ET on September 30. The active month is the November 2026 contract (CLX26), because October CL's last trade was around September 22 and the roll happened around the September 18 session.

In the 22 September sessions listed, the gap between the open and the intraday low was more than $4 in about 5 of them: Sep 16 (−4.5), Sep 21 (−5.6), Sep 22 (−3.3), Sep 29 (−5.0) and Sep 11 (−5.8). That shows swings of about 5% within a single session are common this month. Sep 30 began near $89.04.

market.question: 0 ships transit Hormuz on any date by September 30?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a daily number of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Strait of Hormuz equal to 0 for any date between market creation and the specified date, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No."

Transit calls include container, dry bulk, roll-on/roll-off, general cargo, and tanker ships. Ships not reported by IMF PortWatch will not be considered.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a daily number of transit calls equal to 0, or once complete data has been published for the specified period without such a publication. If complete data for the specified period has not been published within 28 calendar days of the end of the specified period, this market will resolve based on data published up to that point.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after the date on which such data is first released to allow for corrections. Data integrity issues refer only to clerical or other similar errors in the underlying data, and do not include cases where IMF PortWatch differs from alternative sources. Revisions to previously published data points made within this market’s timeframe will be considered. However, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying except in the case of data integrity issues. 

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the transit calls data published for the Strait of Hormuz at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/cb5856222a5b4105adc6ee7e880a1730, both in the chart and through downloadable files.

recent_facts.fact: The latest IMF PortWatch data point is for 2026-09-27, when 1 vessel transited the Strait of Hormuz. The pre-crisis baseline is about 85 per day. The brief does not report any zero-transit day in the recent data.
IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit through Hormuz on 2026-09-20. This was described as the lowest single-day count since the conflict began, apart from the zero days in March.
PortWatch has recorded 3 zero-transit days for Hormuz since 2026-03-01, all in March 2026 right after the strait was closed. The seven years of the series before that contain none.
IMF PortWatch recorded 8 transits on 2026-09-13 and 6 transits on 2026-09-06, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.
As of 2026-09-20, the 7-day average of PortWatch transits was about 3 per day, roughly 3% of normal.

IMF PortWatch publishes weekly, on Tuesdays, with about a two-day lag, so the newest Hormuz data is usually 2 to 9 days old. Data for 2026-09-28 to 2026-09-30 would be expected in the Tuesday 2026-10-06 update, which falls inside the market's 28-day window for complete data.

A non-PortWatch tracker counted 17 vessels transiting Hormuz on 2026-09-28 (11 inbound, 6 outbound), down from 24 the day before. It also noted that many tankers cross with their AIS transponders switched off.
A commodity-vessel tracker counted 10 crossings on 2026-09-23, up from 7 on 2026-09-22, against a 10-day average of about 17. Other trackers count differently from PortWatch.

An unidentified tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on 2026-09-28. Mediators were still pursuing a US-Iran deal, but Iran's UN delegation said it had no plans for more meetings, and US Ambassador Mike Waltz dismissed Iran's proposal.
A Kuwaiti KOTC tanker was reported struck in the Strait of Hormuz. US-Iran talks remain stalled after the US rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the strait.
In early September the US struck Iranian oil tankers for the first time, in retaliation for Iranian attacks, and the exchanges of fire in the strait continued through the month.

PortWatch data for 2026-09-28, 09-29 and 09-30 is still unpublished. These are the last dates that count toward the question.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if any Binance 1 minute candle for SOL/USDT from the creation of this market through 11:59 PM ET on the last day of the month specified in the title has a final Low price equal to or lower than the price specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". Price action before this market's creation will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is Binance, specifically the SOL/USDT Low prices available at https://www.binance.com/en/trade/SOL_USDT, with the chart settings on "1m" for one-minute candles selected on the top bar.

Please note that the outcome of this market depends solely on the price data from the Binance SOL/USDT trading pair. Prices from other exchanges, different trading pairs, or spot markets will not be considered for the resolution of this market.

market.question: Will Russia enter Mykolaivka by September 30, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Mykolaivka, Donetsk Oblast, (48.854785° N, 37.770676° E) between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The boundaries of the municipality are those shown under the “Ukrainian Settlements” layer on the ISW map.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded under a qualifying layer on the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

ISW described this as 'an area where Russian forces previously conducted an infiltration mission.' So Russian troops had been inside the town's eastern part at some point before September 26. From the text alone it is unclear whether or when this was shaded as an infiltration area on the ISW map.

recent_facts.fact: The same report's lines about Mykolaivka as a 'gray zone' and Russian forces likely not holding consolidated positions in 'Mykolaivka or Podilske' concern a different Mykolaivka, just west of Chasiv Yar. It is not the Slovyansk-area town at 48.85N, 37.77E. Do not mix up the two when reading ISW text.

DeepState's Roman Pohorilyi said Russian troops were 'now infiltrating Mykolaivka,' a key strongpoint on the approach to Sloviansk. He said this followed Moscow moving forces south after Ukraine's Operation Vivaldi counteroffensive (Sept 15–20) stopped the Russian advance north of Lyman.

By early August 2026, Russia was attacking Mykolaivka, which Euromaidan called 'the gateway to Sloviansk,' with Ukraine's 81st brigade defending. The town sits about 8 km east of Sloviansk, and taking it is described as a precondition for any Russian siege of the city.
Russian Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov claimed in late August 2026 that Russian troops were 4 km from Slovyansk's eastern outskirts.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

market.question: Will Likud win the most seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are expected to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party or coalition that wins the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of this election.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties or coalitions for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose candidate list received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed name appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Israeli Knesset.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Israel’s Central Election Committee (Va'adet HaBehirot HaMerkazit) (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/central-elections-committee/govil-landing-page).

The following rules govern the merging, joint contention, and splitting of listed parties:

- If Likud or Together (or any successor party created through a merger) merge with or contest the election jointly with any other party, the option corresponding to Likud or Together will represent the resultant candidate list or merged party. 

Otherwise:

- If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more unlisted parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list. If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more other listed parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the party which held the most seats in the prior Knesset will represent all seats won by the merged party/joint candidate list. If these rules do not adequately determine which option represents a merged party or joint candidate list, the listed party whose name, as listed in this market, comes first in alphabetical order, will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list.

- If a listed party splits into multiple parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent the resulting party that holds the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of the split. If these rules do not adequately determine which party represents a listed option after a split, the listed option will represent all seats won by the party resulting from the split whose primary English name comes first in alphabetical order.

The Bears lost 9-3 to the Vikings at Soldier Field in Week 2, for 12 total points. Williams was hurt during the game.

The Jets lost 20-17 in overtime to the Packers in Week 2, for 37 total points.
The Jets beat the Titans 23-10 in Week 1, for 33 total points. Smith went 19 of 24 for 215 yards with no interceptions.

market.question: Will Russia enter Mykolaivka by September 30, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Mykolaivka, Donetsk Oblast, (48.854785° N, 37.770676° E) between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The boundaries of the municipality are those shown under the “Ukrainian Settlements” layer on the ISW map.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded under a qualifying layer on the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

recent_facts.fact: ISW reported that Ukrainian forces cleared a Russian position in eastern Mykolaivka (east of Slovyansk), based on geolocated footage published September 26. ISW called it 'an area where Russian forces previously conducted an infiltration mission.' The report does not say when that infiltration happened.
ISW reported that Russian forces kept up offensive operations east of Slovyansk toward Mykolaivka on September 27 and 28 but did not advance, and that Ukrainian forces counterattacked in the area.

ISW said Ukrainian forces are advancing toward Rai-Oleksandrivka (southeast of Mykolaivka) but have not yet cleared the forest north of that village. Russian forces are attacking toward Mykolaivka from that forest.

ISW's late-September reports also cover a different Mykolaivka just west of Chasiv Yar, which ISW describes as a contested 'gray zone' where neither side likely holds consolidated positions. That village is not the one at the question's coordinates (48.85° N, 37.77° E, east of Slovyansk).

DeepState's Roman Pohorilyi said Russian troops 'are now infiltrating Mykolaivka,' a key strongpoint on the approach to Sloviansk. After a Ukrainian counteroffensive north of Lyman, Russia shifted forces south of Lyman toward Mykolaivka.

DeepState said the Mykolaivka–Orikhuvata–Nykonorivka line is the last important defensive line before possible direct fighting for Sloviansk. It said Russian forces stepped up assaults south of Lyman, aiming to reach the Raihorodok area.
DeepState reported Russian advances near Mykolaivka and Dovha Balka in Donetsk Oblast. The date is approximate; the article falls in the September 2026 reporting period.
On August 13, ISW noted a Russian milblogger's claim that Russian forces advanced east of Mykolaivka (east of Slovyansk). ISW gave no geolocated confirmation.

By early August 2026, Russia was assaulting Mykolaivka, the 'gateway to Sloviansk,' which Ukraine's 81st brigade was defending. Search summaries say Russian forces had infiltrated Pyskunivka and Mykolaivka near Slovyansk in August 2026.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $95 in September?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of September 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.source: Investing.com (Crude Oil WTI Futures historical data)
recent_facts.fact: Investing.com's daily WTI futures data puts the lowest September 2026 low at $86.13, on September 1. Every other September session's low was $88.58 or higher. None of the daily lows for September 1–30 reached $85. This is continuous front-month data, not Pyth 1-minute candles.
On September 29, WTI opened at $93.53 and traded between $94.72 and $88.58 before closing at $89.05. That $88.58 low was the lowest level since the September 1 session.

The August 31 session had a low of $84.11 and closed at $85.76. The September 1 session, which starts at 6 PM ET on August 31, opened at $86.31 and bottomed at $86.13. So the sub-$85 trade happened in an August session, before September's trading began.

On September 30, oil steadied after its biggest drop in more than a week. WTI was slipping toward $89 and Brent was near $103. Middle East crude exports had rebounded to 17.5 million barrels a day, 98% of pre-war levels.
On September 28, WTI settled at $92.60 after reaching $96.54 intraday. Prices came off their highs on reports that Saudi Arabia was ramping its East-West pipeline back up after repairs.

WTI's September peak was a high of $105.63 on September 16. The price then fell to around $89–92 in the last two weeks of the month, as U.S.-Iran truce hopes and a recovery in Saudi supply weighed on it.

Only one session is left: September 30, which ends at 5:00 PM ET. The market closes at 03:59:59 UTC on October 1, which is 11:59 PM ET on September 30. The active month is the November 2026 contract (CLX26), because October CL's last trade was around September 22 and the roll happened around the September 18 session.

market.question: Will the U.S. and China agree to establish an AI hotline before Oct 1, 2026? (Before Oct 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If the governments of the United States and China have formally announced an agreement to establish, or have implemented, a bilateral notification mechanism for AI incidents that could affect national security after Issuance and before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify, unless the new article itself explicitly reaffirms the truth of the topic as of the publication date. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

A qualifying mechanism must be a government-to-government arrangement for notifying the other government about relevant AI incidents; general AI dialogue, shared principles, safety cooperation, or a general hotline without the incident-notification function does not satisfy this topic.

The mechanism must be expressly described in an official government announcement, agreement text, or qualifying Source Agency report as covering AI incidents with national-security implications. A general AI-incident channel does not qualify based solely on an inference that the incidents it covers could affect national security.

A formal announcement must appear in an official agreement text, communiqué, readout, press release, other written government statement, or a formal government press conference, briefing, leaders' summit, signing ceremony, or formal address. One government's official statement is sufficient only when it expressly states that both governments agreed. Informal remarks, press gaggles, a report of a proposal, an agreement to meet, or a transcript of those remarks alone does not qualify.

Implementation requires evidence that both governments have operationalized, activated, or used the bilateral notification mechanism. A unilateral proposal, ongoing negotiation, planned dialogue, generic AI-safety principles, company standards, private or unofficial arrangement, domestic-only system, or a mechanism unrelated to AI incidents affecting national security does not qualify. A broader AI-safety agreement qualifies only when it expressly adopts or implements this incident-notification component.

recent_facts.fact: On September 18, 2026, Trump said on Truth Social that he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters from the White House. The White House defended Trump calling Bloomberg reporter Catherine Lucey "piggy" on Air Force One in November 2025. That remark is his main widely reported use of the word as an insult.
In the days after the "piggy" remark, Trump insulted other female reporters with words like "ugly," "stupid" and "terrible person." These reports do not show him repeating "piggy."

Trump has long called the US a "piggy bank" on trade. At a May 2019 rally in Panama City Beach he called America "the piggy bank that everybody wants to rob." Saying "piggy bank" would include the word "piggy."

At the June 2018 G7 summit, Trump said the US is "the piggy bank that everybody's robbing." He has used the "piggy bank" phrase repeatedly when talking about trade and tariffs, including a later post about foreign digital taxes making Silicon Valley the world's "piggy bank" (Gizmodo).

About two days are left before the deadline of October 1, 2026 at 12:00am ET. Any public remark, published direct quote or Truth Social or X post by Trump counts, and so do plural or possessive forms.

market.question: Will Russia enter Mykolaivka by September 30, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Mykolaivka, Donetsk Oblast, (48.854785° N, 37.770676° E) between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The boundaries of the municipality are those shown under the “Ukrainian Settlements” layer on the ISW map.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded under a qualifying layer on the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

recent_facts.fact: ISW reported that Ukrainian forces cleared a Russian position in eastern Mykolaivka (east of Slovyansk), based on geolocated footage published September 26. ISW called it 'an area where Russian forces previously conducted an infiltration mission.' The report does not say when that infiltration happened.
ISW reported that Russian forces kept up offensive operations east of Slovyansk toward Mykolaivka on September 27 and 28 but did not advance, and that Ukrainian forces counterattacked in the area.

ISW said Ukrainian forces are advancing toward Rai-Oleksandrivka (southeast of Mykolaivka) but have not yet cleared the forest north of that village. Russian forces are attacking toward Mykolaivka from that forest.

ISW's late-September reports also cover a different Mykolaivka just west of Chasiv Yar, which ISW describes as a contested 'gray zone' where neither side likely holds consolidated positions. That village is not the one at the question's coordinates (48.85° N, 37.77° E, east of Slovyansk).

DeepState's Roman Pohorilyi said Russian troops 'are now infiltrating Mykolaivka,' a key strongpoint on the approach to Sloviansk. After a Ukrainian counteroffensive north of Lyman, Russia shifted forces south of Lyman toward Mykolaivka.

DeepState said the Mykolaivka–Orikhuvata–Nykonorivka line is the last important defensive line before possible direct fighting for Sloviansk. It said Russian forces stepped up assaults south of Lyman, aiming to reach the Raihorodok area.
DeepState reported Russian advances near Mykolaivka and Dovha Balka in Donetsk Oblast. The date is approximate; the article falls in the September 2026 reporting period.
On August 13, ISW noted a Russian milblogger's claim that Russian forces advanced east of Mykolaivka (east of Slovyansk). ISW gave no geolocated confirmation.

By early August 2026, Russia was assaulting Mykolaivka, the 'gateway to Sloviansk,' which Ukraine's 81st brigade was defending. Search summaries say Russian forces had infiltrated Pyskunivka and Mykolaivka near Slovyansk in August 2026.

facts_dropped.fact: The question closes at 11:59 PM ET on September 30, 2026, so only ISW's September 29–30 map updates remain. Qualifying shading (infiltration, advance or control layers) must persist through the next full daily update. Whether ISW's earlier infiltration shading in eastern Mykolaivka fell after the market was created, and lasted a full update cycle, could not be confirmed directly from the map.

market.rules:

The word or phrase must be stated by President Donald Trump in public statements, direct quotes published by Source Agencies, or written public statements on his personal social media accounts (Twitter/Truth Social). Official acts like Executive Orders or bills signed do not count. The exact phrase/word, or a plural or possessive form of the phrase/word, must be used. Grammatical/tense inflections are otherwise not included. 
For phrases with slashes like "Doge/Dogecoin," either word satisfies the criterion. If the word must be said a minimum number of times, all instances must occur after market issuance.
Please see full rules for more details.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia – Donald Trump's conflict with the news media
recent_facts.fact: On September 26, 2026, Trump told a female MS NOW reporter she was "fake news" and "MS DNC" and told her to "be quiet." The report does not say he used the word "piggy."

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia – Donald Trump's conflict with the news media
recent_facts.fact: On September 18, 2026, Trump said on Truth Social that he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico reporters from the White House. On September 21 the outlets sued, and on September 23 Judge Timothy J. Kelly granted a 14-day temporary restraining order restoring their credentials. On September 24 Trump barred CNN from Air Force One.

A Daily Kos community post titled "Little Sensitive Piggy" was published on September 21, 2026. The article text could not be retrieved, and nothing available shows that Trump himself said "piggy" at the time.
The White House defended Trump calling Bloomberg reporter Catherine Lucey "piggy" on Air Force One in November 2025. That remark is his main widely reported use of the word as an insult.
In the days after the "piggy" remark, Trump insulted other female reporters with words like "ugly," "stupid" and "terrible person." These reports do not show him repeating "piggy."

Trump has long called the US a "piggy bank" on trade. At a May 2019 rally in Panama City Beach he called America "the piggy bank that everybody wants to rob." Saying "piggy bank" would include the word "piggy."

At the June 2018 G7 summit, Trump said the US is "the piggy bank that everybody's robbing." He has used the "piggy bank" phrase repeatedly when talking about trade and tariffs, including a later post about foreign digital taxes making Silicon Valley the world's "piggy bank" (Gizmodo).

About two days are left before the deadline of October 1, 2026 at 12:00am ET. Any public remark, published direct quote or Truth Social or X post by Trump counts, and so do plural or possessive forms.

recent_facts.fact: India won the 1st ODI in Thiruvananthapuram by 8 wickets. West Indies made 295/7, including Justin Greaves' maiden ODI century, and Virat Kohli's 139* took India to the target in 41.4 overs. India lead the three-match series 1-0.

Sherfane Rutherford missed the 1st ODI for personal reasons and is set to rejoin the West Indies squad for the 2nd ODI.

Across 142 ODIs between the sides, India have won 72 and West Indies 64, with 2 ties and 4 no results. This appears to be the record before the 1st ODI of this series.

In ODIs played in India, India lead West Indies 32 wins to 28 across 61 matches, with 1 tie. Four of the five lowest team totals in this fixture belong to West Indies, including 104 all out at Thiruvananthapuram in 2018.

West Indies' last ODI win in India was by 8 wickets in Chennai on December 15, 2019. India have won every home ODI against West Indies since then, including the 2022 series and the 1st ODI on September 27, 2026.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (Sri Lankan cricket team in West Indies in 2026)
recent_facts.fact: In West Indies' previous ODI series, at home against Sri Lanka in June–July 2026, Sri Lanka won 1-0. Sri Lanka won the 1st ODI by 41 runs, and the 2nd and 3rd ODIs were abandoned without a ball bowled.

Shai Hope captains West Indies and Shubman Gill captains India. The West Indies ODI squad includes Roston Chase, Alzarri Joseph, Shamar Joseph, Gudakesh Motie, Keemo Paul and Sherfane Rutherford, with Jewel Andrew replacing the injured Ackeem Auguste.

recent_facts.fact: The Yankees beat the Red Sox 4-0 in Game 1 of the best-of-three AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on Sept. 29, 2026. New York leads the series 1-0 and needs one more win to advance.

Since the best-of-three Wild Card format began in 2022, Game 1 winners have won 15 of 16 series. The one exception was 2025, when the Yankees lost Game 1 to Boston and came back to win the series 2-1.
All games are at Yankee Stadium. Game 2 is Max Fried (NYY) vs. Sonny Gray (BOS). If needed, Game 3 is Gerrit Cole (NYY) vs. Ranger Suarez (BOS). The winner plays the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
Game 2 is set for Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026 at 8 p.m. ET on NBC/Peacock. As of the latest search results it had not been played. Game 3, if needed, would follow on Oct. 1.
Aaron Judge was left off the Yankees' Wild Card Series roster. He has been on the injured list with a calf strain since Sept. 16.
Red Sox injury concerns before the series: Willson Contreras has a hand injury after being hit by a pitch, and Ceddanne Rafaela has a quad strain and hamstring cramp.

The Yankees won the 2026 regular-season series against Boston 7-6. Season stats for the Game 2 starters: Fried 2.80 ERA over 112.2 IP; Gray 2.72 ERA over 169.0 IP. Game 3 starters: Cole 3.61 ERA over 127.0 IP; Suarez 3.22 ERA over 148.1 IP.
The Yankees are the AL's top wild-card seed, reported at 93-68, the second-best record in the AL. Boston had the third-best AL record (Fox Sports).

In Game 1, Cam Schlittler threw 117 pitches over six-plus innings, striking out 10, and allowed one hit through six. Ben Rice homered. Boston starter Payton Tolle went 4 2/3 innings and allowed one run.
In the 2025 AL Wild Card Series, the Yankees beat the Red Sox 2-1, winning Game 2 4-3 and Game 3 4-0 after losing Game 1.
