market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by October 5, 2026?
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of the listed countries is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $85 in September?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of September 2026, any 1-minute candle for the Active Month of WTI Crude Oil futures has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered. The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 6:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date. Under the standard schedule, trading is open from 6:00:00 PM ET Sunday through 5:00:00 PM ET Friday, with a daily break from 5:00:00 PM ET to 6:00:00 PM ET, except where modified by holiday or special-session hours.

The active month changes at the start of the second trading session prior to the nearest listed contract's last trading session. At that point, the next listed contract becomes the active month (i.e., for the final three trading sessions of the nearest listed contract, the contract for the next month is the active month).

Per CME contract specifications for WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures, a contract's last trading day is three business days prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract's delivery month (or four business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a business day).

For example, if the 25th of the month is a Saturday, the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Tuesday the 21st, and the next listed contract becomes the active month at the start of the trading session for Friday the 17th (6:00 PM ET on Thursday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other technical disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil (CL) futures contract by CME Group may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session.

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the Active Month WTI Crude Oil futures "High" and "Low" prices available at https://pythdata.app/explore?search=WTI, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.fact: Investing.com's daily WTI futures data puts the lowest September 2026 low at $86.13, on September 1. Every other September session's low was $88.58 or higher. None of the daily lows for September 1–30 reached $85. This is continuous front-month data, not Pyth 1-minute candles.
Early on September 30, WTI futures were at $89.06, with a session range so far of $89.00–$89.06. That is about $4 (roughly 4.5%) above $85.
On September 29, WTI opened at $93.53 and traded between $94.72 and $88.58 before closing at $89.05. That $88.58 low was the lowest level since the September 1 session.

The August 31 session had a low of $84.11 and closed at $85.76. The September 1 session, which starts at 6 PM ET on August 31, opened at $86.31 and bottomed at $86.13. So the sub-$85 trade happened in an August session, before September's trading began.

On September 30, oil steadied after its biggest drop in more than a week. WTI was slipping toward $89 and Brent was near $103. Middle East crude exports had rebounded to 17.5 million barrels a day, 98% of pre-war levels.

On September 29, WTI fell about 3.5% to around $89.38 and Brent fell 2.6% to $102.59. The drop came as Saudi crude exports from its Red Sea ports recovered after an attack on a key pipeline earlier in the month.
On September 28, WTI settled at $92.60 after reaching $96.54 intraday. Prices came off their highs on reports that Saudi Arabia was ramping its East-West pipeline back up after repairs.

WTI's September peak was a high of $105.63 on September 16. The price then fell to around $89–92 in the last two weeks of the month, as U.S.-Iran truce hopes and a recovery in Saudi supply weighed on it.

Only one session is left: September 30, which ends at 5:00 PM ET. The market closes at 03:59:59 UTC on October 1, which is 11:59 PM ET on September 30. The active month is the November 2026 contract (CLX26), because October CL's last trade was around September 22 and the roll happened around the September 18 session.

market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 15?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported that flows through the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea had reached at least 3.5 million b/d after repairs, about half of its 7 million b/d capacity. The report adds that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Saudi Aramco had made any public statement on the pipeline since the attack. The information came from people familiar with the matter.

The article's timeline gives the restart on September 22, 2026 at minimal capacity, citing unnamed Reuters sources, and says full recovery could take 6 to 8 weeks. It cites no Ministry of Energy, Saudi Press Agency (SPA) or Energy Minister statement about the restart.

Three unnamed sources said Saudi Arabia had restarted the East-West Pipeline, which was pumping at a low rate, and that exports from Yanbu could resume. Aramco did not comment, and a security source said a full resumption could take weeks. Before the shutdown the line carried about 4 million b/d.
Bloomberg reported that Saudi Aramco was running tests and building pressure on the East-West pipeline with the aim of restoring significant flows by the end of that week.

Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia had resumed crude loadings at Yanbu after the pipeline restart, averaging about 2 million b/d since the previous week. The report is based on sources and tracking data, not an official government statement.

The Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West Pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after multiple attacks on the morning of September 10 in the Riyadh and Madinah regions. This is the official announcement the question refers to.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright called the Saudi pipeline closure a brief interruption that would last days. This is a US official's statement, not a Saudi government one.

After attacks on a pumping station in April 2026 cut East-West throughput by 700,000 b/d, the Saudi Ministry of Energy issued a public SPA statement on April 12, 2026 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has formally announced a pipeline restoration before.

Only an official Saudi government announcement that the pipeline is currently operating (partial capacity counts) qualifies. Media reports citing unnamed sources, Aramco tests, or tanker-tracking data showing flows do not count unless the government itself says the pipeline is operating.
The window for a qualifying Saudi government announcement closes October 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. As of September 28 reporting, no official statement on the restart had been found.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

market.question: Will Likud win the most seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are expected to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party or coalition that wins the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of this election.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties or coalitions for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose candidate list received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed name appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Israeli Knesset.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Israel’s Central Election Committee (Va'adet HaBehirot HaMerkazit) (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/central-elections-committee/govil-landing-page).

The following rules govern the merging, joint contention, and splitting of listed parties:

- If Likud or Together (or any successor party created through a merger) merge with or contest the election jointly with any other party, the option corresponding to Likud or Together will represent the resultant candidate list or merged party. 

Otherwise:

- If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more unlisted parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list. If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more other listed parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the party which held the most seats in the prior Knesset will represent all seats won by the merged party/joint candidate list. If these rules do not adequately determine which option represents a merged party or joint candidate list, the listed party whose name, as listed in this market, comes first in alphabetical order, will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list.

- If a listed party splits into multiple parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent the resulting party that holds the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of the split. If these rules do not adequately determine which party represents a listed option after a split, the listed option will represent all seats won by the party resulting from the split whose primary English name comes first in alphabetical order.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The boundaries of the municipality are those shown under the “Ukrainian Settlements” layer on the ISW map.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded under a qualifying layer on the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by October 5, 2026?
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

Only reporting from any of the Source Agencies qualifies for the purposes of this market. Reports that merely reference prior publications (from before Issuance) do not qualify, unless the new article itself explicitly reaffirms the truth of the topic as of the publication date. Republishing of content originally produced by other sources (e.g., wire services) only qualifies if the content is hosted on the outlet's official platform and the outlet is clearly identified as the publishing entity.

A qualifying mechanism must be a government-to-government arrangement for notifying the other government about relevant AI incidents; general AI dialogue, shared principles, safety cooperation, or a general hotline without the incident-notification function does not satisfy this topic.

The mechanism must be expressly described in an official government announcement, agreement text, or qualifying Source Agency report as covering AI incidents with national-security implications. A general AI-incident channel does not qualify based solely on an inference that the incidents it covers could affect national security.

A formal announcement must appear in an official agreement text, communiqué, readout, press release, other written government statement, or a formal government press conference, briefing, leaders' summit, signing ceremony, or formal address. One government's official statement is sufficient only when it expressly states that both governments agreed. Informal remarks, press gaggles, a report of a proposal, an agreement to meet, or a transcript of those remarks alone does not qualify.

Implementation requires evidence that both governments have operationalized, activated, or used the bilateral notification mechanism. A unilateral proposal, ongoing negotiation, planned dialogue, generic AI-safety principles, company standards, private or unofficial arrangement, domestic-only system, or a mechanism unrelated to AI incidents affecting national security does not qualify. A broader AI-safety agreement qualifies only when it expressly adopts or implements this incident-notification component.

recent_facts.fact: On the resolution source's own page, Digger (2026) had a 52% Tomatometer from 111 reviews. The Popcornmeter showed 0 verified ratings.

Digger goes into wide theatrical release on October 2, 2026. The question resolves on the Tomatometer at 10:00 AM ET on Monday, Oct 5, 2026, and the score must be strictly above 45 (46% or higher) for Yes.
At 12:51 PM EDT on Sept 29, MovieWeb reported a 52% Tomatometer from 67 reviews, making it Iñárritu's lowest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes.
A later report put the score at 53% from 99 reviews. It called this Cruise's worst critical reception since The Mummy (2017, 15%).

Digger debuted at a 41% Tomatometer on its first batch of reviews. As more reviews came in, reports put it anywhere from 41% to 54%, and it has since settled around 51–53% at 95–111 reviews.
Digger was reported at a 42 Metascore on Metacritic alongside the 52% Tomatometer. Critics called it a 'shallow satire' but praised Cruise's performance and the production design.
The film opens nationwide October 2 on a reported $130M budget, with a projected $23M domestic opening. More reviews are likely to be added between now and the Oct 5 resolution time.

As the review count grew from 67 to 111, the score stayed between 51% and 54%. With 111 reviews at 52%, about 58 are positive. To fall to 45% or below, roughly 18 of the next 20 new reviews (or 31 of the next 40) would have to be negative.

Vučić heads the SNS-led 'United Serbia' list, ahead of Miloš Vučević and Ana Brnabić. The other main lists are the Student List 'Students Are Winning', Ivica Dačić's SPS-led 'Factor of Stability', European Serbia and the Authentic Right. The question counts only a Prime Minister elected by the National Assembly and sworn in. Macut's cabinet continuing in office, or any caretaker, does not count. market.question: Saudi Oil Pipeline (East-West) restarts by October 15?
market.rules:
On September 11, 2026, Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West oil pipeline has been shut down.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the government of Saudi Arabia announces that the East-West oil pipeline is operational or no longer shut down between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must express that the pipeline is presently operating; operation at partial or reduced capacity qualifies.

Announcements that attribute such a claim to third parties, state that the pipeline will or may operate in the future, describe work underway to restore operation, or frame resumption as expected, planned, or conditional, will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of any subsequent contradictory statements, or alternative information from other sources.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the government of Saudi Arabia.

recent_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported that flows through the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea had reached at least 3.5 million b/d after repairs, about half of its 7 million b/d capacity. The report adds that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Saudi Aramco had made any public statement on the pipeline since the attack. The information came from people familiar with the matter.

The article's timeline gives the restart on September 22, 2026 at minimal capacity, citing unnamed Reuters sources, and says full recovery could take 6 to 8 weeks. It cites no Ministry of Energy, Saudi Press Agency (SPA) or Energy Minister statement about the restart.

Three unnamed sources said Saudi Arabia had restarted the East-West Pipeline, which was pumping at a low rate, and that exports from Yanbu could resume. Aramco did not comment, and a security source said a full resumption could take weeks. Before the shutdown the line carried about 4 million b/d.
Bloomberg reported that Saudi Aramco was running tests and building pressure on the East-West pipeline with the aim of restoring significant flows by the end of that week.

Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia had resumed crude loadings at Yanbu after the pipeline restart, averaging about 2 million b/d since the previous week. The report is based on sources and tracking data, not an official government statement.

The Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West Pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after multiple attacks on the morning of September 10 in the Riyadh and Madinah regions. This is the official announcement the question refers to.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright called the Saudi pipeline closure a brief interruption that would last days. This is a US official's statement, not a Saudi government one.

After attacks on a pumping station in April 2026 cut East-West throughput by 700,000 b/d, the Saudi Ministry of Energy issued a public SPA statement on April 12, 2026 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has formally announced a pipeline restoration before.

Only an official Saudi government announcement that the pipeline is currently operating (partial capacity counts) qualifies. Media reports citing unnamed sources, Aramco tests, or tanker-tracking data showing flows do not count unless the government itself says the pipeline is operating.
The window for a qualifying Saudi government announcement closes October 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. As of September 28 reporting, no official statement on the restart had been found.

An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: The reimposed US naval blockade of Iranian ports began July 14, 2026, after Trump announced it on July 13. The article says it is still in effect, with no end date announced.
Trump publicly rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, saying "They made a proposal but I rejected it." Iran's price for reopening included an end to the US naval blockade.

Iran's plan would reopen Hormuz within 7 days if the US lifts the blockade, waives sanctions, releases $12bn in frozen assets and agrees to a regional ceasefire that includes Lebanon. The US wants all issues, including nuclear, settled together rather than step by step. Araghchi said Iran's position has not changed, and no formal next meeting has been announced.

On September 30, Iran was reported to have received Washington's response to its seven-point proposal through Qatari mediators. The main dispute is said to be the order of steps in the 7-day framework, and the White House is reported to be tempering expectations of an imminent breakthrough.
Reports said Trump expects to resume bombing Iran after the early-November US midterm elections. Officials said he has not made an irrevocable decision to restart major combat.

Trump posted on Truth Social "I offered them NOTHING!" A US official said sanctions relief is possible if there is concrete progress on nuclear issues, but the two sides disagree on timing. The US also imposed new sanctions on Iranian military suppliers.
Axios reported that Trump is willing to ease sanctions and unfreeze assets in exchange for nuclear concessions from Iran. The full article could not be accessed.

Precedent: the first blockade (April 13 to June 18) ended when Trump announced a deal on June 14, signed an MOU on June 17, and CENTCOM formally announced the blockade's removal on June 18. It lasted about 2 months, and the lifting came only as part of a signed war-ending agreement.
By September 12, CENTCOM said it had redirected more than 100 vessels. The WSJ reported in early September that the blockade had halted new Iranian oil exports from the Persian Gulf.

On September 5, the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier and a destroyer enforcing the blockade; CENTCOM said neither was hit. Iran threatened more severe attacks if the blockade continues and on September 6 announced a "restricted zone" running south of Hormuz.

No formal US-Iran negotiating session is scheduled before the October 15 deadline. Indirect talks run through Qatar, and the US midterms, which Trump has linked to the timing of a deal, fall in early November, after the question closes.

market.question: Will OpenAI release a personal AI agent before Oct 1, 2026? (Before Oct 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If an OpenAI product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

market.question: Will the unemployment rate (U-3) be above 3.9% in September? (Above 3.9%)
market.rules: If the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (U-3) reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics in the Employment Situation Report is above 3.9% in September 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.

recent_facts.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation Summary (August 2026)
recent_facts.fact: The seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1% in August 2026, with 7.0 million people unemployed. For the September figure to be 3.9% or lower, the rate would have to fall by at least 0.2 percentage points in one month.

Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August 2026, compared with an average gain of 31,000 a month over the prior 12 months. Unemployment rates were 4.0% for adult men, 3.5% for adult women and 14.1% for teenagers.
Labor force participation edged up to 61.6% in August 2026, still below January's level. June and July payrolls were revised up by a combined 55,000.

The unemployment rate fell from 4.2% in June to 4.1% in July 2026 even though payrolls fell by 23,000. The drop came mainly from people leaving the labor force: participation fell to 61.4%, its lowest in more than five years.
Bloomberg described 4.1% as a one-year low for the unemployment rate, meaning the rate has not been below 4.1% at any point in the past year.
Initial jobless claims were 197,000 for the week ending September 19, 2026, down from 198,000 the week before. Continuing claims fell to 1.719 million.
Jobless claims fell to 196,000 during the holiday week, which included the September CPS survey reference week around September 12. Continuing claims also dropped.
The September 2026 Employment Situation report is scheduled for Friday, October 2, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET (12:30 UTC). The question closes one minute earlier, at 12:29 UTC.

The House passed a continuing resolution 370-48, and the Senate had earlier passed it 90-6. It funds the government through December 11, 2026, and was signed into law, so there is no shutdown on October 1 to delay the BLS release (unlike the October 2025 shutdown, which cancelled the October 2025 household survey).
BLS publishes U-3 rounded to one decimal place, from the household survey (CPS). 'Above 3.9%' therefore resolves Yes if the published September rate is 4.0% or higher.

recent_facts.fact: No. 7 Alabama (4-0, 2-0 SEC) plays at No. 16 Mississippi State (4-0, 2-0 SEC) on Saturday, Oct 3, 2026, at Davis Wade Stadium in Starkville, with a 12 p.m. EDT kickoff.

Through the 2023 season, Alabama led the all-time series 86-18-3 (88-17-3 on the field, but two Alabama wins were vacated or forfeited). Mississippi State's last win in the series was 17-12 on Nov 10, 2007. Alabama won every meeting from 2009 to 2023, and 13 of those 15 wins were by 10 points or more.
WTVA reports Mississippi State has not beaten Alabama in 19 years, and the Bulldogs are trying to end that streak on Saturday.
Mississippi State has won only 5 of the 26 games against Alabama played in Starkville.

The closest recent meetings were Alabama 31-24 (2017), 25-20 (2014) and 24-24... correction: 25-20 (2014) and 31-24 (2017) are the only games since 2009 decided by 7 points or fewer. Alabama's other wins in that stretch included 49-9 (2021), 41-0 (2020) and 30-6 (2022). Scores for 2024 and later were not on the page.

Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor threw for 360 yards and 3 TDs, including a go-ahead 24-yard TD to Sanfrisco Magee with 3:57 left, as then-No. 24 MSU beat No. 19 Missouri 31-24. It is the program's first set of back-to-back 4-0 starts since 1944-45.

Kamario Taylor left the Missouri game with an apparent injury, came out of the medical tent after a few minutes, threw on the sideline and returned to finish the game. No MSU injury report for the Alabama game was found.
Then-No. 8 Alabama beat South Carolina 49-18. QB Keelon Russell threw for 365 yards and 4 TDs and ran for another score.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team)
recent_facts.fact: Mississippi State's 2026 results: beat UL Monroe 62-13, won at Minnesota 38-13, won at South Carolina 41-34, beat No. 19 Missouri 31-24.
Alabama is 4th nationally in scoring at 48.0 points per game and Mississippi State is 15th at 43.0. Russell is 78 of 110 passing with 8 TD and 2 INT. Taylor is 83 of 120 with 14 TD and 2 INT.

Alabama injuries: RT Jayvin James (lower extremity) is 'very much questionable,' and freshman Tyrell Miller filled in against South Carolina. LG Will Sanders (upper body) is expected to play, per Kalen DeBoer.

Alabama edge rushers Justin Hill (lower extremity, out several weeks) and Desmond Umeozulu (turf toe, 'out for a bit' per DC Kane Wommack) are expected to miss the game. Zavier Mincey was hurt before the South Carolina game, and WR A. Walker's status is uncertain.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $95 in September?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of September 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Will Russia enter Mykolaivka by September 30, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures any territory of Mykolaivka, Donetsk Oblast, (48.854785° N, 37.770676° E) between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

Territory will be considered captured if any part of the specified territory is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

The boundaries of the municipality are those shown under the “Ukrainian Settlements” layer on the ISW map.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date.

Any continuous shading under the following layers will qualify:
- Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas
- Assessed Russian-Controlled Terrain
- Assessed Russian Advances

Shading under the following layers will not qualify:
- Claimed Russian Territory

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded under a qualifying layer on the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by October 5, 2026?
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of the listed countries is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will OpenAI release a personal AI agent before Oct 1, 2026? (Before Oct 1, 2026)
market.rules:
If an OpenAI product has implemented a general-purpose personal AI agent that remembers the user and starts multi-step tasks across third-party apps on its own before Oct 1, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The function must be live and processing user interactions, not explicitly labeled as "beta," "test," "experimental," "preview," or "early access" or similar, and officially acknowledged by the company through announcements, documentation, or help pages. Implementation includes direct integration into the product's interface, automatic application to user accounts, user-initiated activation through official controls, API implementation, or policy changes that operationally enforce the function. Announcements without deployment, employee-only testing, technical documentation without implementation, and third-party additions without authorization do not qualify. The implementation must occur in the United States unless otherwise specified. If it meets these conditions, it counts from the first date it is live for users outside the company, including in a gradual rollout or a waitlist, invitation-only, or paid-tier release.

A general-purpose personal AI agent acts for an individual user on that user's own goals, is not limited to a single category of task or app, such as only code, only documents, or only shopping, and (1) retains user-specific information, such as preferences, relationships, goals, or ongoing activities, across separate interactions, and (2) as a built-in capability, on its own initiative and outside any conversation or task the user has started, begins new multi-step actions across third-party apps, websites, or services to advance the user's ongoing goals, based on what it has retained. The agent must itself take at least one such action before asking the user anything, and may then pause for approval before a step such as sending a message or making a purchase. An action means changing something in a third-party app, website, or service on the user's behalf, such as sending, posting, booking, purchasing, submitting a form, or creating, editing, or deleting an item; reading, searching, or summarizing does not count. An agent focused on work qualifies if it acts across email, calendar, messaging, and the web for an individual user.

The following do not qualify: carrying out a task the user started, however long-running; running tasks on a user-defined schedule, event trigger, or monitor, or under a standing instruction that tells the agent what to do or which app, source, or workflow to watch; a briefing or notification on its own; a proposed task or suggestion that does nothing until the user accepts it; an offer made in reply to the user's message; memory alone; an agent configured by an organization to run shared team workflows; and a developer platform, SDK, or API for building agents, unless the company itself offers through it an agent that meets (1) and (2) for end users. A goal or preference the user has shared, from which the agent itself decides what new task to start, is not a standing instruction, and neither is turning the capability on, connecting apps, or granting permissions.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: The reimposed US naval blockade of Iranian ports began July 14, 2026, after Trump announced it on July 13. The article says it is still in effect, with no end date announced.
Trump publicly rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, saying "They made a proposal but I rejected it." Iran's price for reopening included an end to the US naval blockade.

Iran's plan would reopen Hormuz within 7 days if the US lifts the blockade, waives sanctions, releases $12bn in frozen assets and agrees to a regional ceasefire that includes Lebanon. The US wants all issues, including nuclear, settled together rather than step by step. Araghchi said Iran's position has not changed, and no formal next meeting has been announced.

On September 30, Iran was reported to have received Washington's response to its seven-point proposal through Qatari mediators. The main dispute is said to be the order of steps in the 7-day framework, and the White House is reported to be tempering expectations of an imminent breakthrough.
Reports said Trump expects to resume bombing Iran after the early-November US midterm elections. Officials said he has not made an irrevocable decision to restart major combat.

Trump posted on Truth Social "I offered them NOTHING!" A US official said sanctions relief is possible if there is concrete progress on nuclear issues, but the two sides disagree on timing. The US also imposed new sanctions on Iranian military suppliers.
Axios reported that Trump is willing to ease sanctions and unfreeze assets in exchange for nuclear concessions from Iran. The full article could not be accessed.

Precedent: the first blockade (April 13 to June 18) ended when Trump announced a deal on June 14, signed an MOU on June 17, and CENTCOM formally announced the blockade's removal on June 18. It lasted about 2 months, and the lifting came only as part of a signed war-ending agreement.
By September 12, CENTCOM said it had redirected more than 100 vessels. The WSJ reported in early September that the blockade had halted new Iranian oil exports from the Persian Gulf.

On September 5, the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier and a destroyer enforcing the blockade; CENTCOM said neither was hit. Iran threatened more severe attacks if the blockade continues and on September 6 announced a "restricted zone" running south of Hormuz.

No formal US-Iran negotiating session is scheduled before the October 15 deadline. Indirect talks run through Qatar, and the US midterms, which Trump has linked to the timing of a deal, fall in early November, after the question closes.

recent_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported that flows through the East-West pipeline to the Red Sea had reached at least 3.5 million b/d after repairs, about half of its 7 million b/d capacity. The report adds that neither the Saudi Energy Ministry nor Saudi Aramco had made any public statement on the pipeline since the attack. The information came from people familiar with the matter.

The article's timeline gives the restart on September 22, 2026 at minimal capacity, citing unnamed Reuters sources, and says full recovery could take 6 to 8 weeks. It cites no Ministry of Energy, Saudi Press Agency (SPA) or Energy Minister statement about the restart.

Three unnamed sources said Saudi Arabia had restarted the East-West Pipeline, which was pumping at a low rate, and that exports from Yanbu could resume. Aramco did not comment, and a security source said a full resumption could take weeks. Before the shutdown the line carried about 4 million b/d.
Bloomberg reported that Saudi Aramco was running tests and building pressure on the East-West pipeline with the aim of restoring significant flows by the end of that week.

Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia had resumed crude loadings at Yanbu after the pipeline restart, averaging about 2 million b/d since the previous week. The report is based on sources and tracking data, not an official government statement.

The Ministry of Energy announced that the East-West Pipeline had been shut down as a precaution after multiple attacks on the morning of September 10 in the Riyadh and Madinah regions. This is the official announcement the question refers to.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright called the Saudi pipeline closure a brief interruption that would last days. This is a US official's statement, not a Saudi government one.

After attacks on a pumping station in April 2026 cut East-West throughput by 700,000 b/d, the Saudi Ministry of Energy issued a public SPA statement on April 12, 2026 that full pumping capacity of about 7 million b/d had been restored. This shows the ministry has formally announced a pipeline restoration before.

Only an official Saudi government announcement that the pipeline is currently operating (partial capacity counts) qualifies. Media reports citing unnamed sources, Aramco tests, or tanker-tracking data showing flows do not count unless the government itself says the pipeline is operating.
The window for a qualifying Saudi government announcement closes October 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. As of September 28 reporting, no official statement on the restart had been found.

recent_facts.fact: On the resolution source's own page, Digger (2026) had a 52% Tomatometer from 111 reviews. The Popcornmeter showed 0 verified ratings.

Digger goes into wide theatrical release on October 2, 2026. The question resolves on the Tomatometer at 10:00 AM ET on Monday, Oct 5, 2026, and the score must be strictly above 45 (46% or higher) for Yes.
At 12:51 PM EDT on Sept 29, MovieWeb reported a 52% Tomatometer from 67 reviews, making it Iñárritu's lowest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes.
A later report put the score at 53% from 99 reviews. It called this Cruise's worst critical reception since The Mummy (2017, 15%).
The review embargo lifted on Tuesday, Sept 29. Coverage that day reported a 53% 'rotten' Tomatometer from 95 reviews and described the reviews as 'brutally split'.
Digger debuted at a 41% Tomatometer on its first batch of reviews. As more reviews came in, reports put it anywhere from 41% to 54%, and it has since settled around 51–53% at 95–111 reviews.
Digger was reported at a 42 Metascore on Metacritic alongside the 52% Tomatometer. Critics called it a 'shallow satire' but praised Cruise's performance and the production design.
The film opens nationwide October 2 on a reported $130M budget, with a projected $23M domestic opening. More reviews are likely to be added between now and the Oct 5 resolution time.

As the review count grew from 67 to 111, the score stayed between 51% and 54%. With 111 reviews at 52%, about 58 are positive. To fall to 45% or below, roughly 18 of the next 20 new reviews (or 31 of the next 40) would have to be negative.

market.question: Will the unemployment rate (U-3) be above 3.9% in September? (Above 3.9%)
market.rules: If the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate (U-3) reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics in the Employment Situation Report is above 3.9% in September 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.

recent_facts.source: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation Summary (August 2026)
recent_facts.fact: The seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1% in August 2026, with 7.0 million people unemployed. For the September figure to be 3.9% or lower, the rate would have to fall by at least 0.2 percentage points in one month.

Nonfarm payrolls rose 162,000 in August 2026, compared with an average gain of 31,000 a month over the prior 12 months. Unemployment rates were 4.0% for adult men, 3.5% for adult women and 14.1% for teenagers.
Labor force participation edged up to 61.6% in August 2026, still below January's level. June and July payrolls were revised up by a combined 55,000.

The unemployment rate fell from 4.2% in June to 4.1% in July 2026 even though payrolls fell by 23,000. The drop came mainly from people leaving the labor force: participation fell to 61.4%, its lowest in more than five years.
Bloomberg described 4.1% as a one-year low for the unemployment rate, meaning the rate has not been below 4.1% at any point in the past year.
Initial jobless claims were 197,000 for the week ending September 19, 2026, down from 198,000 the week before. Continuing claims fell to 1.719 million.
Jobless claims fell to 196,000 during the holiday week, which included the September CPS survey reference week around September 12. Continuing claims also dropped.
The September 2026 Employment Situation report is scheduled for Friday, October 2, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET (12:30 UTC). The question closes one minute earlier, at 12:29 UTC.

The House passed a continuing resolution 370-48, and the Senate had earlier passed it 90-6. It funds the government through December 11, 2026, and was signed into law, so there is no shutdown on October 1 to delay the BLS release (unlike the October 2025 shutdown, which cancelled the October 2025 household survey).
BLS publishes U-3 rounded to one decimal place, from the household survey (CPS). 'Above 3.9%' therefore resolves Yes if the published September rate is 4.0% or higher.

recent_facts.fact: Tyrrell Hatton, ranked 24th in the world (OWGR), is in the 168-player field for the 2026 Alfred Dunhill Links Championship, which has a $5,000,000 purse. The field includes seven players from the world top 50: Fitzpatrick (4), Fleetwood (9), Rose (16), MacIntyre (19), Noren (21), Hatton (24) and Straka (35).

The event is a pro-am, with each team made up of one amateur and one professional, played across three courses. After 54 holes the top 60 professionals and the leading 20 pro-am teams advance to the final round at St Andrews. Under the market rules, a Hatton withdrawal or non-start before teeing off resolves No.

market.question: Will Yashar win the most seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are expected to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the political party or coalition that wins the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of this election.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

In the event of a tie between multiple parties or coalitions for the most seats won, this market will resolve in favor of the party or coalition whose candidate list received a greater number of valid votes. In the event that results in a tie, this market will resolve in favor of the party whose listed name appears first in alphabetical order.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named party or coalition in the Israeli Knesset.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Israel’s Central Election Committee (Va'adet HaBehirot HaMerkazit) (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/central-elections-committee/govil-landing-page).

The following rules govern the merging, joint contention, and splitting of listed parties:

- If Likud or Together (or any successor party created through a merger) merge with or contest the election jointly with any other party, the option corresponding to Likud or Together will represent the resultant candidate list or merged party. 

Otherwise:

- If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more unlisted parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list. If a listed party merges with, or contests the election as part of a joint candidate list with, one or more other listed parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the party which held the most seats in the prior Knesset will represent all seats won by the merged party/joint candidate list. If these rules do not adequately determine which option represents a merged party or joint candidate list, the listed party whose name, as listed in this market, comes first in alphabetical order, will represent all seats won by the merged party or joint candidate list.

- If a listed party splits into multiple parties prior to the election, the option corresponding to the listed party will represent the resulting party that holds the greatest number of seats in the Israeli Knesset as a result of the split. If these rules do not adequately determine which party represents a listed option after a split, the listed option will represent all seats won by the party resulting from the split whose primary English name comes first in alphabetical order.

market.question: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 25 bps after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: On the resolution source's own page, Digger (2026) had a 52% Tomatometer from 111 reviews. The Popcornmeter showed 0 verified ratings.

Digger goes into wide theatrical release on October 2, 2026. The question resolves on the Tomatometer at 10:00 AM ET on Monday, Oct 5, 2026, and the score must be strictly above 45 (46% or higher) for Yes.
At 12:51 PM EDT on Sept 29, MovieWeb reported a 52% Tomatometer from 67 reviews, making it Iñárritu's lowest-rated film on Rotten Tomatoes.
A later report put the score at 53% from 99 reviews. It called this Cruise's worst critical reception since The Mummy (2017, 15%).
The review embargo lifted on Tuesday, Sept 29. Coverage that day reported a 53% 'rotten' Tomatometer from 95 reviews and described the reviews as 'brutally split'.
Digger debuted at a 41% Tomatometer on its first batch of reviews. As more reviews came in, reports put it anywhere from 41% to 54%, and it has since settled around 51–53% at 95–111 reviews.
Digger was reported at a 42 Metascore on Metacritic alongside the 52% Tomatometer. Critics called it a 'shallow satire' but praised Cruise's performance and the production design.
The film opens nationwide October 2 on a reported $130M budget, with a projected $23M domestic opening. More reviews are likely to be added between now and the Oct 5 resolution time.

As the review count grew from 67 to 111, the score stayed between 51% and 54%. With 111 reviews at 52%, about 58 are positive. To fall to 45% or below, roughly 18 of the next 20 new reviews (or 31 of the next 40) would have to be negative.

recent_facts.fact: The Yankees beat the Red Sox 4-0 in Game 1 of the best-of-three AL Wild Card Series at Yankee Stadium on Sept. 29, 2026. New York leads the series 1-0 and needs one more win to advance.

Since the best-of-three Wild Card format began in 2022, Game 1 winners have won 15 of 16 series. The one exception was 2025, when the Yankees lost Game 1 to Boston and came back to win the series 2-1.
All games are at Yankee Stadium. Game 2 is Max Fried (NYY) vs. Sonny Gray (BOS). If needed, Game 3 is Gerrit Cole (NYY) vs. Ranger Suarez (BOS). The winner plays the Tampa Bay Rays in the ALDS.
Game 2 is set for Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026 at 8 p.m. ET on NBC/Peacock. As of the latest search results it had not been played. Game 3, if needed, would follow on Oct. 1.
Aaron Judge was left off the Yankees' Wild Card Series roster. He has been on the injured list with a calf strain since Sept. 16.
Red Sox injury concerns before the series: Willson Contreras has a hand injury after being hit by a pitch, and Ceddanne Rafaela has a quad strain and hamstring cramp.

The Yankees won the 2026 regular-season series against Boston 7-6. Season stats for the Game 2 starters: Fried 2.80 ERA over 112.2 IP; Gray 2.72 ERA over 169.0 IP. Game 3 starters: Cole 3.61 ERA over 127.0 IP; Suarez 3.22 ERA over 148.1 IP.
